# Sirius SQL reference

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate_sql_reference.py from a Sirius build; do not edit. -->

Table functions and settings the Sirius CUDA backend registers, as `duckdb_functions()` and `duckdb_settings()` report them. The `sirius` loader adds `sirius_status()`, described in [sirius-duckdb/README.md](../sirius-duckdb/README.md). Some settings also have `sirius.yaml` counterparts; see the [configuration reference](super-sirius/configuration.md).

## Table functions

### Execution

#### `gpu_execution(sql VARCHAR, enable_optimizer BOOLEAN, query_label VARCHAR)`

Runs a SQL query on the GPU with Sirius and returns its result. While the gpu_execution setting is true (the default) Sirius already runs supported queries on the GPU transparently, so this is only needed to run one query explicitly. sql must be exactly one SQL statement, normally a SELECT query. If GPU execution fails, the query is run again on DuckDB's CPU engine unless enable_duckdb_fallback is false; queries that read s3:// have no CPU fallback. Named parameters: query_label (VARCHAR) names the query in Sirius telemetry and takes precedence over sirius_set_query_label; enable_optimizer (BOOLEAN, default true) set to false skips DuckDB's optimizer for the plan Sirius runs, a debugging aid under which more queries fall back to the CPU.

```sql
SELECT * FROM gpu_execution('SELECT l_returnflag, sum(l_quantity) AS sum_qty FROM lineitem GROUP BY l_returnflag ORDER BY l_returnflag');
SELECT * FROM gpu_execution('SELECT count(*) FROM read_parquet(''lineitem/*.parquet'')', query_label => 'lineitem_count');
SELECT * FROM gpu_execution('SELECT count(*) FROM lineitem', enable_optimizer => false);
```

### Pinned tables and caches

#### `pin_table(path VARCHAR, tier VARCHAR, name VARCHAR, cols VARCHAR[], compression BOOLEAN, format VARCHAR, schema_name VARCHAR)`

Pins Parquet files (a path or glob) in GPU memory, pinned host memory or the I/O cache, so later Sirius queries over the same files skip reading them, and with tier 'gpu' or 'host' decoding them too. Named parameters: name (VARCHAR, required) is the key unpin_table takes, while queries find the pin by its files; tier (VARCHAR, required) is 'gpu' or 'host' for decoded columns, or 'parquet' for the undecoded column chunks, which needs sirius.executor.scan_manager.cache.mode 'cucs' in the Sirius config and stays pinned only with cache eviction 'lru' and eviction_threshold_fraction 1.0; cols (VARCHAR[]) pins only these columns (default all); compression (BOOLEAN, default the pin_table_compression setting) compresses the pin when pin_table_input_compression_plan_dir holds a plan for name; format (VARCHAR) is 'parquet' or 'duckdb' and is inferred from a .parquet, .db or .duckdb suffix when omitted, and format 'duckdb' pins the DuckDB table called name, as the form without a path does. Returns one row with Success = true.

```sql
CALL pin_table('lineitem/*.parquet', name => 'lineitem', tier => 'gpu');
CALL pin_table('lineitem/*.parquet', name => 'lineitem', tier => 'host', cols => ['l_orderkey', 'l_quantity', 'l_extendedprice']);
CALL pin_table('lineitem/*.parquet', name => 'lineitem_bytes', tier => 'parquet');
```

#### `pin_table(tier VARCHAR, name VARCHAR, cols VARCHAR[], compression BOOLEAN, format VARCHAR, schema_name VARCHAR)`

Pins a table of a file-backed DuckDB database in GPU or pinned host memory, so later Sirius queries that scan it skip reading and decoding it. Pass format => 'duckdb'. Named parameters: name (VARCHAR, required) is the table, optionally qualified, and the key to unpin it with; tier (VARCHAR, required) is 'gpu' or 'host'; schema_name (VARCHAR, default 'main') is the schema of an unqualified name, resolved through DuckDB's catalog search path; cols (VARCHAR[]) pins only these columns (default all); compression (BOOLEAN, default the pin_table_compression setting) compresses the pin when pin_table_input_compression_plan_dir holds a plan for name. Run CHECKPOINT after loading the table and before pinning it. Pinning turns off automatic WAL checkpoints for the whole DuckDB instance, and unpin_table does not turn them back on. Returns one row with Success = true.

```sql
CALL pin_table(name => 'orders', format => 'duckdb', tier => 'gpu');
CALL pin_table(name => 'lineitem', format => 'duckdb', tier => 'host', cols => ['l_orderkey', 'l_quantity']);
```

#### `reset_sirius_cache()`

Drops and rebuilds Sirius's prefetching I/O caches so that the next query reads its data from storage again, for cold-cache benchmarks. Parquet-tier pins (pin_table tier => 'parquet') are dropped with the cache; GPU and host pins are kept. Returns one row with Success = true.

```sql
CALL reset_sirius_cache();
```

#### `sirius_analyze_parquet(path VARCHAR)`

Reads the footer statistics of the Parquet files matching a path or glob into Sirius's process-wide cache, so the first multi-file scan of them can give DuckDB's optimizer their merged column statistics (see the parquet_footer_statistics setting) without reading every footer while planning. Returns one row with files (UBIGINT), the number of matching files, cached ones included. Errors if no file matches. Only scans with DuckDB's default Parquet options reuse these statistics, and only while a file is unchanged; a local file modified moments ago is read but not cached.

```sql
SELECT files FROM sirius_analyze_parquet('lineitem/*.parquet');
```

#### `unpin_table(name VARCHAR)`

Releases a pin that pin_table made under the given name, freeing its GPU, host or I/O cache memory; an unknown name is not an error. ANN indexes built on the table keep their GPU memory until sirius_drop_ann_index drops them, and a re-pinned table needs its index rebuilt. Returns one row with Success = true.

```sql
CALL unpin_table('lineitem');
```

### Vector search

#### `sirius_create_ann_index(table_name VARCHAR, column_name VARCHAR, metric VARCHAR, index_type VARCHAR, n_lists BIGINT, schema_name VARCHAR)`

Builds a GPU IVF-Flat approximate nearest neighbor index on a FLOAT[N] column of a DuckDB table pinned with pin_table tier => 'gpu', for sirius_knn_search; it replaces an index on the same column and metric. Named parameters: metric (VARCHAR) is 'l2' (default) or 'cosine'; n_lists (BIGINT) is the number of IVF lists, 0 (default) for min(1024, sqrt(rows)); index_type (VARCHAR) is 'ivf_flat' (the default and only type); schema_name (VARCHAR, default 'main') is the schema of an unqualified table. Returns one row with Success = true.

```sql
CALL sirius_create_ann_index('items', 'embedding');
CALL sirius_create_ann_index('items', 'embedding', metric => 'cosine', n_lists => 64);
```

#### `sirius_drop_ann_index(table_name VARCHAR, column_name VARCHAR, metric VARCHAR, schema_name VARCHAR)`

Drops the ANN indexes sirius_create_ann_index built on a column and frees their GPU memory: with metric (VARCHAR, 'l2' or 'cosine') only that metric's index, otherwise the index of every metric. schema_name (VARCHAR, default 'main') is the schema of an unqualified table. Returns one row with Dropped = true if an index was removed.

```sql
CALL sirius_drop_ann_index('items', 'embedding');
CALL sirius_drop_ann_index('items', 'embedding', metric => 'cosine');
```

#### `sirius_knn_search(table_name VARCHAR, column_name VARCHAR, query ANY, k BIGINT, output_columns VARCHAR[], metric VARCHAR, use_index BOOLEAN, n_probes BIGINT, index_type VARCHAR, schema_name VARCHAR)`

Returns up to k rows of a GPU-pinned DuckDB table whose FLOAT[N] column is nearest to a query vector, nearest first, each followed by its distance (FLOAT). query is a FLOAT[N] array or a list of N numbers. Named parameters: k (BIGINT, default 10); output_columns (VARCHAR[], default every pinned column) are the columns returned before distance; metric (VARCHAR) is 'l2' (Euclidean distance, default) or 'cosine' (cosine distance); use_index (BOOLEAN, default true) searches the index sirius_create_ann_index built for the metric, and false searches exactly; n_probes (BIGINT) is the number of IVF lists searched, 0 (default) for min(n_lists, 32); index_type (VARCHAR) is 'ivf_flat' (the default and only type); schema_name (VARCHAR, default 'main') is the schema of an unqualified table. Index searches with metric 'cosine' allow k up to 256.

```sql
SELECT * FROM sirius_knn_search('items', 'embedding', [0.1, 0.2, 0.3]::FLOAT[3], k => 5);
SELECT id, distance FROM sirius_knn_search('items', 'embedding', [0.1, 0.2, 0.3]::FLOAT[3], k => 20, metric => 'cosine', use_index => false, output_columns => ['id']);
```

### Telemetry

#### `sirius_set_query_label(label VARCHAR)`

Names the next query Sirius runs on this connection in Sirius telemetry (Quent); the label applies to that one query, and queries without a label are recorded as unnamed_query. A gpu_execution call takes the label when it is bound (prepared), and a query_label passed to it takes precedence. Returns one row with ok = true.

```sql
CALL sirius_set_query_label('tpch_q1');
```

#### `sirius_set_session_label(label VARCHAR)`

Groups the following Sirius queries on this connection under one telemetry query group (Quent) until the label is changed; an empty string restores the default group. Returns one row with ok = true.

```sql
CALL sirius_set_session_label('nightly_tpch');
CALL sirius_set_session_label('');
```

### Developer

#### `profiler_start()`

Starts CUDA profiler data collection (cudaProfilerStart), so that nsys profile --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi records only what runs until profiler_stop(); a developer tool. Returns one row with ok = true.

```sql
CALL profiler_start();
```

#### `profiler_stop()`

Stops CUDA profiler data collection (cudaProfilerStop), ending the range profiler_start() began for nsys profile --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi; a developer tool. Returns one row with ok = true.

```sql
CALL profiler_stop();
```

### Internal

#### `sirius_read_parquet(uri VARCHAR)`

Internal: the Sirius scan of S3 Parquet that gpu_execution puts in place of read_parquet('s3://...'), so the query binds through Sirius's own S3 reader; not meant to be called directly, and DuckDB cannot execute it. Query S3 Parquet with read_parquet('s3://...') instead.

```sql
SELECT * FROM gpu_execution('SELECT count(*) FROM read_parquet(''s3://my-bucket/events/part-0.parquet'')');
```

#### `sirius_stream_source(stream_id BIGINT)`

Internal: stands in for input stream stream_id of a Sirius fragment plan, which the GPU plan replaces with a streaming source; not meant to be called directly. It binds only to a stream declared on the connection, returning that stream's columns, and DuckDB cannot execute it.

```sql
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW main.sirius_stream_0 AS SELECT * FROM sirius_stream_source(0);
```

## Settings

Set with `SET name = value;`.

| Setting | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `admission_bytes_per_gpu` | UBIGINT | Estimated scan output in bytes per GPU, used to choose how many GPUs a query runs on, up to sirius.topology.gpus_per_query in sirius.yaml. 0 uses every GPU that gpus_per_query allows. |
| `avg_variable_column_bytes` | UBIGINT | Assumed size in bytes of each value of a variable-width column, such as VARCHAR or LIST, when estimating scan output for admission_bytes_per_gpu. Must be greater than 0; unused when admission_bytes_per_gpu is 0. |
| `enable_compressed_materialization` | BOOLEAN | Whether pin_table stores integer and DECIMAL columns in the narrowest type that holds their values, to save memory. Query results are unchanged, and tables pinned earlier keep their storage. |
| `enable_duckdb_fallback` | BOOLEAN | Whether to run a query on DuckDB's CPU engine when the GPU cannot plan or execute it. When false, such queries fail with the GPU error. Queries that read s3:// paths through Sirius never fall back. |
| `expression_evaluator_strategy` | VARCHAR | How the GPU evaluates expressions: 'ast_interpret' runs each expression tree in one interpreted kernel, 'ast_jit' compiles expression trees into kernels at runtime, and 'materialize' computes each operation into an intermediate column. |
| `gpu_execution` | BOOLEAN | Whether to transparently run supported queries on the GPU. When false, queries run on DuckDB's CPU engine unless passed to the gpu_execution table function. |
| `hash_partition_bytes` | UBIGINT | Target size in bytes, greater than 0, of one hash partition in GPU joins and aggregations; smaller values lower peak GPU memory per task but create more tasks. Defaults to 1/40 of the smallest GPU's memory, clamped to 512 MiB-5 GiB; a GPU memory limit in sirius.yaml can lower it. |
| `max_broadcast_join_size` | UBIGINT | Largest build side in bytes that a hash join copies to every GPU, instead of partitioning it across GPUs, when the probe side is much larger. Build sides under 16 MiB per GPU are eligible regardless. |
| `max_sort_partition_bytes` | UBIGINT | Target size in bytes of one ORDER BY partition on the GPU, used to choose how many partitions a sort splits into. 0 derives it from max_sort_partition_memory_fraction of the GPU memory available when the sort starts. |
| `max_sort_partition_memory_fraction` | DOUBLE | Fraction of the available GPU memory, from 0 to 1, used as the target ORDER BY partition size when max_sort_partition_bytes is 0. 0 sorts the whole input as one partition. |
| `parquet_footer_statistics` | BOOLEAN | Whether to give DuckDB's optimizer column statistics merged from the footers of all files in a multi-file Parquet scan, for better filter and join estimates. DuckDB itself reads them only with union_by_name. |
| `pin_table_compression` | BOOLEAN | Whether pin_table compresses a table when its compression parameter is omitted. Compression needs a plan file for the table in pin_table_input_compression_plan_dir; tables without one are pinned uncompressed. |
| `pin_table_compression_max_compressed_fraction` | DOUBLE | Largest compressed size, as a fraction of the uncompressed size, at which pin_table keeps a batch compressed; otherwise the batch is pinned uncompressed. 0.75 requires at least 25% savings, and values above 1 accept compressed batches that grew. |
| `pin_table_compression_min_batch_size_bytes` | UBIGINT | Minimum uncompressed size in bytes of a batch for pin_table to compress it; smaller batches are pinned uncompressed. |
| `pin_table_input_compression_plan_dir` | VARCHAR | Directory of compression plan files for pin_table, one per table, named after pin_table's name parameter with any extension. Tables without a plan file are pinned uncompressed; empty disables pin_table compression. |
| `pin_table_prove_unique_keys` | BOOLEAN | Whether pin_table checks which integer columns of pinned Parquet files have no duplicate values, so joins on them can use the faster hash join for unique keys, as with a PRIMARY KEY. When false, joins also ignore uniqueness found by earlier pins. |
| `pin_table_unique_exact_max_bytes` | UBIGINT | Maximum GPU memory in bytes that pin_table keeps, across all columns, for its exact uniqueness check; peak use is about three times this. 0 uses 10% of the GPU memory Sirius manages. |
| `sirius_log_backend` | VARCHAR | Where Sirius writes its log: 'spdlog' to daily files sirius_YYYY-MM-DD.log in sirius_log_dir, 'duckdb' to DuckDB's log with type 'Sirius', or 'noop' nowhere. Applies to the whole process; defaults to the SIRIUS_LOG_BACKEND environment variable when set. |
| `sirius_log_dir` | VARCHAR | Directory of the Sirius log files, one per day named sirius_YYYY-MM-DD.log, when sirius_log_backend is 'spdlog'; relative paths resolve against the working directory. Applies to the whole process; defaults to the SIRIUS_LOG_DIR environment variable when set. |
| `sirius_log_flush_seconds` | INTEGER | Seconds between automatic flushes of the Sirius log file when sirius_log_backend is 'spdlog'; 0 disables periodic flushing. Applies to the whole process. |
| `sirius_log_level` | VARCHAR | Minimum level of Sirius log messages: trace, debug, info, warn, error, critical or off. The 'duckdb' backend uses DuckDB's log level instead. Applies to the whole process; defaults to the SIRIUS_LOG_LEVEL environment variable when set. |
| `spill_compression` | BOOLEAN | Whether to compress batches spilled to host memory or disk, and decompress them when they are loaded back. Applies to the whole process, not just this session. |

## Tuning settings

Low-level knobs, hidden from `duckdb_settings()` unless called with `debug := true`; they can still be set.

| Setting | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `dynamic_filter_domain_coverage_threshold` | DOUBLE | Skip runtime join filters on a join key that is unique in its table when the join's build side keeps at least this fraction of that table's rows, since such filters remove few rows. Must be greater than 0; values above 1 never skip. |
| `dynamic_filter_inlist_max_l2_fraction` | DOUBLE | Largest exact-match runtime join filter, as a fraction of the GPU's L2 cache size from 0 to 1; larger key sets use a Bloom filter. 0 uses a Bloom filter whenever possible, except for very small key sets. |
| `dynamic_filter_keep_threshold` | DOUBLE | Stop applying runtime join filters to a scan once together they keep more than this fraction of its rows, from 0 to 1, until new filters arrive. 1 disables this cutoff; single filters that keep most rows can still be skipped. |
| `enable_regex_jit_impl` | BOOLEAN | Whether regexp_replace with the pattern '^https?://(?:www\\.)?([^/]+)/.*$' and the replacement '\\1' uses a hand-written GPU kernel instead of cuDF's regex engine. No other pattern is affected. |
| `enable_runtime_size_estimation` | BOOLEAN | Whether grouped aggregations choose their partition count from a projected input size instead of waiting for all of their input, so they can start sooner. Experimental. |
| `like_swar_fastpath` | BOOLEAN | Whether LIKE and NOT LIKE patterns made of literals separated and surrounded by %, such as '%abc%def%', use a specialized GPU kernel instead of cuDF's general LIKE. |
| `mark_join_build_switch_ratio` | DOUBLE | For mark joins, which evaluate some IN and EXISTS subqueries, build the hash table on the left side when the right side has at least this many times more rows. 0 always builds on the right side. The best value depends on the GPU. |
| `max_build_hash_table_bytes` | UBIGINT | Maximum estimated hash table size in bytes per GPU, at 16 bytes per build row, for a hash join to build its table once and reuse it for every probe batch; 0 disables reusable builds. Defaults to 8 times hash_partition_bytes as configured at startup. |
| `max_build_probe_resident_bytes` | UBIGINT | Maximum build-side data in bytes per GPU that a hash join reusing one build table may keep in GPU memory, unspillable, while it probes; 0 disables reusable builds. Defaults to 1/5 of the smallest GPU's memory, clamped to 4-40 GiB; a GPU memory limit in sirius.yaml can lower it. |
| `sort_sample_bytes` | UBIGINT | Bytes of ORDER BY input to collect before choosing the sort's partition boundaries; 0 uses only the first batch. Defaults to 1/40 of the smallest GPU's memory, clamped to 512 MiB-5 GiB; a GPU memory limit in sirius.yaml can lower it. |
| `use_hw_decompression` | BOOLEAN | Whether Parquet scans use the GPU's hardware decompression engine when every GPU supports it. Read-only: set sirius.operator_params.use_hw_decompression in sirius.yaml instead. |

| Setting | Type | Description |
